system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Mexico City, Mexico. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Mexico City itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Mexico City space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Colonia Juárez/Cuauhtémoc, San Miguel Chapultepec, Roma/Condesa, Polanco, San Rafael/Santa María la Ribera, Escandón, San Ángel/Coyoacán) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Mexico City spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Mexico City, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Kurimanzutto
galleries.note: Mexico’s most internationally influential contemporary gallery, with a generation-defining roster and sustained blue-chip institutional and fair presence.

galleries.name: OMR
galleries.note: A cornerstone of Mexico City’s gallery scene, known for ambitious exhibitions, major Latin American artists and exceptional international reach.

galleries.name: LABOR
galleries.note: Critically rigorous gallery focused on research-led, political and conceptual practices with strong museum recognition.

galleries.name: Gaga
galleries.note: Highly influential gallery linking Mexico City with international experimental art through a tightly edited, critically followed programme.

galleries.name: Proyectos Monclova
galleries.note: Major contemporary gallery combining internationally established artists, historical research and prominent art-fair participation.

galleries.name: joségarcía, mx
galleries.note: A leading platform for conceptually sharp emerging and mid-career artists from Mexico and abroad.

galleries.name: Galerie Nordenhake México
galleries.note: The Mexico City branch of the influential European gallery contributes a museum-level international programme and significant fair presence.

galleries.name: Travesía Cuatro
galleries.note: An important transatlantic gallery with a strong Latin American roster and regular participation in leading global fairs.

galleries.name: Galería de Arte Mexicano (GAM)
galleries.note: Founded in 1935, Mexico’s foundational modern gallery remains relevant through contemporary exhibitions, estates and unmatched historical continuity.

galleries.name: RGR
galleries.note: Internationally visible gallery connecting geometric abstraction’s historical legacies with prominent contemporary Latin American practices.

galleries.name: Galería Hilario Galguera
galleries.note: Long-running gallery recognized for large-scale exhibitions, international artists and a substantial presence in Mexico’s art market.

galleries.name: PEANA
galleries.note: A fast-rising gallery with a strong younger roster, sophisticated installations and growing international fair and institutional attention.

galleries.name: Revolver Galería
galleries.note: The Mexico City space of the Lima-founded gallery advances experimental Latin American practices and productive regional exchange.

galleries.name: Arróniz
galleries.note: Established gallery with sustained support for Mexican and Latin American artists and consistent participation in international fairs.

galleries.name: Mariane Ibrahim
galleries.note: The gallery’s permanent Mexico City space brings a globally prominent programme centered on artists of Africa and its diaspora.

galleries.name: Galería Karen Huber
galleries.note: Respected for sustained engagement with contemporary painting and for developing several closely watched Mexican artists.

galleries.name: Proyecto Paralelo
galleries.note: A rigorous gallery known for conceptual, archival and socially attentive practices from Mexico and Latin America.

galleries.name: Galería Agustina Ferreyra
galleries.note: Internationally connected gallery presenting adventurous emerging practices, particularly from Latin America and the Caribbean.

galleries.name: Patricia Conde Galería
galleries.note: Mexico’s leading commercial gallery devoted to photography, with an established roster and strong specialist-fair visibility.

galleries.name: Anonymous Gallery
galleries.note: Independent gallery with a distinctive cross-border programme spanning emerging art, subculture and experimental exhibition formats.

galleries.name: MASA
galleries.note: Globally influential nomadic and permanent platform dissolving distinctions between contemporary art, collectible design and architecture.

galleries.name: AGO Projects
galleries.note: Internationally recognized gallery for collectible design and art, particularly work grounded in Mexican materials and craft knowledge.

galleries.name: SAENGER Galería
galleries.note: Dynamic contemporary gallery with a growing roster and regular appearances at Mexico’s principal and emerging-art fairs.

galleries.name: Galería Mascota
galleries.note: Closely watched gallery presenting emerging international artists through concise, experimental exhibitions.

galleries.name: Lodos
galleries.note: Influential artist-led gallery associated with conceptually adventurous young artists and Mexico City’s independent scene.

galleries.name: General Expenses
galleries.note: Critically regarded independent gallery whose experimental programme gives early support to emerging local and international artists.

galleries.name: Campeche
galleries.note: Artist-founded gallery with an inventive emerging programme and increasing visibility at international young-gallery fairs.

galleries.name: Biquini Wax EPS
galleries.note: Seminal artist-run collective and research space whose exhibitions, library and public discussions have shaped independent discourse.

galleries.name: Salón Silicón
galleries.note: Important queer and feminist artist-run space supporting transgressive practices often underserved by commercial institutions.

galleries.name: Galería Enrique Guerrero
galleries.note: Long-established gallery with a broad Mexican and Latin American roster and decades of art-fair participation.

galleries.name: Pequod Co.
galleries.note: Small but internationally visible gallery known for precise exhibitions by emerging and under-recognized artists.

galleries.name: Le Laboratoire
galleries.note: Established Condesa gallery presenting multidisciplinary Mexican and international contemporary art with a conceptual emphasis.

galleries.name: Galería Alfredo Ginocchio
galleries.note: Veteran commercial gallery with extensive Latin American fair activity and a sizable roster of established artists.

galleries.name: Machete Galería
galleries.note: Known for politically engaged Latin American art and for cultivating artists from across the region.

galleries.name: La Cometa México
galleries.note: The Mexico City location extends an established Latin American gallery network with a strong modern and contemporary programme.

galleries.name: MAIA Contemporary
galleries.note: Polished contemporary programme emphasizing Latin American artists and growing regional and international market visibility.

galleries.name: CAM Galería
galleries.note: Active commercial gallery combining established Mexican artists with newer contemporary positions and regular fair participation.

galleries.name: N.A.S.A.L. México
galleries.note: Cross-Latin American gallery supporting experimental emerging artists through its permanent Mexico City programme.

galleries.name: Deli Gallery
galleries.note: Mexico City branch of the independent gallery, notable for an energetic younger roster and transnational programme.

galleries.name: guadalajara90210
galleries.note: Artist-driven gallery with an irreverent identity, experimental installations and sustained attention from the emerging-art circuit.

galleries.name: Llano
galleries.note: Independent gallery valued for site-responsive exhibitions and its engagement with younger Mexican and international practices.

galleries.name: Fundación Olivia
galleries.note: A newer private foundation and public exhibition space presenting ambitious projects drawn from and developed around its contemporary collection.

galleries.name: FF Projects
galleries.note: Emerging gallery and curatorial platform focused on experimental exhibitions and international exchange.

galleries.name: JO-HS
galleries.note: Gallery and residency platform connecting Mexico City with an international community of emerging artists and curators.

galleries.name: LaNao Galería
galleries.note: Independent gallery recognized for accessible but critically engaged exhibitions by younger Mexican artists.

galleries.name: Arredondo Arozarena
galleries.note: Contemporary gallery with a sustained commitment to emerging and mid-career Latin American artists.

galleries.name: Proyecto H
galleries.note: Mexico–Spain gallery platform with a diverse contemporary roster and regular presence at regional fairs.

galleries.name: Tiro al Blanco México
galleries.note: The gallery’s Mexico City venue broadens its support for emerging Mexican artists beyond its Guadalajara base.

galleries.name: Galería Unión
galleries.note: Independent gallery promoting exchange among artists from Mexico and the wider Latin American scene.

galleries.name: EDS Galería
galleries.note: Established gallery known for contemporary painting, sculpture and multidisciplinary work by Mexican artists.

galleries.name: Galería 54
galleries.note: Condesa gallery providing a visible platform for emerging and mid-career contemporary practices.

galleries.name: Colector
galleries.note: Younger gallery with a collector-facing programme of current Mexican and Latin American art.

galleries.name: Templo
galleries.note: Emerging gallery whose intimate exhibitions contribute to the city’s active younger-gallery ecosystem.

galleries.name: Relaciones Públicas
galleries.note: Independent curatorial and exhibition platform recognized for collaborative, unconventional presentations.

galleries.name: Casa Equis
galleries.note: Gallery and residency that gives artists room for experimentation while building links with local collectors and curators.

galleries.name: Heart Ego
galleries.note: Young gallery presenting intimate exhibitions centered on emerging contemporary voices.

galleries.name: Elipsis
galleries.note: Emerging space notable for compact, conceptually focused exhibitions and participation in the city’s independent art circuit.

galleries.name: Yope Projects
galleries.note: Small artist-centered platform supporting experimental production and exchange among younger practices.

galleries.name: Sismo
galleries.note: New-generation gallery gaining attention for a tightly curated programme and engagement with Mexico City’s artist community.

galleries.name: Can Can
galleries.note: Independent project space adding experimental and collaborative exhibitions to the city’s emerging-art landscape.

galleries.name: Tiempos Modernos
galleries.note: Young curatorial platform known for flexible exhibition formats and participation in alternative art-week programming.

galleries.name: Galería Nina Menocal
galleries.note: Long-running gallery particularly important for its advocacy of Cuban and Latin American contemporary art.

galleries.name: Terreno Baldío Arte
galleries.note: Established Roma gallery with a broad multidisciplinary programme and longstanding ties to Mexican artists.

galleries.name: Galería López Quiroga
galleries.note: Veteran gallery and dealer bridging major modern Mexican names with selected contemporary artists and estates.

galleries.name: Galería Juan Martín
galleries.note: Historic gallery whose decades of work with important Mexican artists give it enduring art-historical significance.

galleries.name: Galería Arvil
galleries.note: One of the city’s long-lived commercial galleries, with deep experience in Mexican modern and contemporary art.

galleries.name: Galería Óscar Román
galleries.note: Established Polanco gallery representing a wide range of Mexican painters, sculptors and mixed-media artists.

galleries.name: ETHRA
galleries.note: Commercial gallery supporting contemporary Mexican artists through exhibitions, commissions and fair participation.

galleries.name: LS/Galería
galleries.note: Gallery with a sustained programme of modern and contemporary Mexican and Latin American work.

galleries.name: Aldama Fine Art
galleries.note: Long-running gallery especially associated with contemporary figurative painting and careful artist development.

galleries.name: Praxis México
galleries.note: Mexico branch of the Latin American gallery network, with decades of activity and a broad regional roster.

galleries.name: Galería Lourdes Sosa
galleries.note: Veteran commercial gallery presenting established Mexican and international contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Aura Galerías
galleries.note: Longstanding gallery with a large collector base and regular exhibitions of Mexican and Latin American art.

galleries.name: ArtSpace México
galleries.note: Commercial platform offering exhibitions and visibility to emerging and mid-career Mexican artists.

galleries.name: Aguafuerte Galería
galleries.note: Accessible Roma gallery with a busy programme of contemporary painting, illustration and graphic work.

galleries.name: Almanaque Fotográfica
galleries.note: Specialist platform supporting contemporary photography through exhibitions, editions and artist-focused projects.

galleries.name: Hydra + Fotografía
galleries.note: Influential photography platform combining exhibitions, publishing, education and an important regional professional network.

galleries.name: Salón de la Plástica Mexicana
galleries.note: Historic artist-membership institution that continues to provide public exhibition space for Mexican visual artists.

galleries.name: Cráter Invertido
galleries.note: Important artist-run collective combining exhibitions, printmaking, publishing and politically engaged collaborative practice.

galleries.name: Aeromoto
galleries.note: Independent public art library and programme that has become a key intellectual resource for artists and researchers.

galleries.name: Archivo Diseño y Arquitectura
galleries.note: Influential research and exhibition space examining modern and contemporary design, architecture and visual culture.

galleries.name: Casa Wabi Santa María

galleries.name: Fundación Alumnos47
galleries.note: Nonprofit foundation supporting experimental education, publishing, public programmes and artist-led contemporary initiatives.

galleries.name: ESPAC

galleries.name: LIGA, Espacio para Arquitectura

galleries.name: Proyector
galleries.note: Independent curatorial space dedicated to critical architectural research, spatial practice and exhibition-making.

galleries.name: La Quiñonera
galleries.note: Legendary artist-run house whose countercultural exhibitions and gatherings have influenced Mexico City art since the 1980s.

galleries.name: Bodega 1249
galleries.note: Independent artist-run venue offering flexible space for experimental exhibitions and collaborative projects.

galleries.name: Vernacular Institute

galleries.name: CC186
galleries.note: Artist-led venue supporting exhibitions, performances and informal exchange outside conventional gallery structures.

galleries.name: Seminario 12
galleries.note: Centro Histórico project space known for context-sensitive exhibitions and collaborations with emerging artists.

galleries.name: Obra Negra
galleries.note: Independent space presenting experimental installations and interdisciplinary work in a raw architectural setting.

galleries.name: ATEA
galleries.note: Collaborative cultural venue hosting exhibitions, performances, workshops and projects by independent creative communities.

galleries.name: Casa Gallina
galleries.note: Locally embedded nonprofit linking contemporary art with food systems, ecology, education and neighborhood participation.

galleries.name: Casa Vecina
galleries.note: Residency and cultural platform with a history of commissioning artists to work with the social fabric of the historic center.

galleries.name: Casa de El Hijo del Ahuizote

galleries.name: Galería Metropolitana (UAM)

galleries.name: Galería José María Velasco

galleries.name: Galería del IFAL

galleries.name: Centro Cultural de España en México
galleries.note: Major public cultural venue whose galleries regularly present contemporary art, media, design and socially engaged projects.
